articles.title: Euro Leagues - Barca the team to stop PSG? Paper planes & Martinez’ apology - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Are Barcelona and PSG the teams to beat in the Champions League?
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 15 Oct 2026 , · 33 mins

Are Barcelona and Paris Saint Germain the teams to beat in the Champions League? Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein are with John Bennett to reflect on their big wins against Galatasaray and Manchester City this week. They debate how Manchester United have handled Lisandro Martinez’ criticism of their technical director Jason Wilcox, after he apologised to the club’s hierarchy for his outburst. Elizabeth Conway joins the pod after paper airplanes and bouncy balls being thrown onto the pitch stopped Rayo Vallecano’s match against Athletic Club. And was Bayern Munich’s draw with Viking the Champions League game of the week? They discuss Michael Olise’s red card and reports that Harry Kane is set to extend his stay at Bayern Munich until 2029. Timecodes: 00:52 - Lisandro Martinez’ apology 06:50 - How good were PSG? 10:06 - Could Barcelona be PSG’s biggest Champions League challengers this season? 19:20 - Paper plane protest at Rayo Vallecano 24:15 - Bayern's draw with Viking 29:27 - Kane set to extend his stay in Munich

articles.title: Mansfield 1-1 Oxford
articles.summary: Oxford clung on for a point with nine men after Michael Smith had rescued a 1-1 draw for Mansfield in a tight encounter.
articles.body:
On a night when Nigel Clough equalled Ian Greaves' record as the club's longest-serving manager, Stags preserved an unbeaten home record stretching back to February.

Luka Lynch had put Oxford ahead with a spectacular first-half goal, but after Peter Kioso was sent off in the 75th minute, Smith levelled matters before Gatlin O'Donkor's red card six minutes from time left the visitors on the ropes.

Lynch took possession on the right of the box and cut inside before curling a superb 18-yard finish under the top-left angle - his first professional goal.

Stags were almost level after 40 minutes. A poor kick by goalkeeper Jamie Cumming saw Stags steal the ball and Smith's shot blocked by Cumming, who was relieved to see Jon Russell put the follow-up over the crossbar.

Liam Roberts stood up well to block when substitute O'Donkor was slipped through by Mo Missanga one-on-one in the 67th minute.

Kioso was dismissed for a second bookable offence - simulation after going down in the box.

And in the 82nd minute Mansfield were level. Stephen McLaughlin sent in an early cross from the left and, as Cumming tried to block, the ball somehow went in off Smith at the near post.

Oxford were reduced to nine men as O'Donkor's foul on Regan Hendry saw him shown a second yellow card.

But, under intense pressure, they hung on to see out seven added minutes.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Soccer coach with unreal eye discipline goes viral for locked in interview with busty reporter
articles.summary: David Oulehla's viral interview with reporter Sabina Jaksova has nearly two million views on FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem's TikTok account page.
articles.body: If this soccer coach doesn’t deserve a lifetime contract, I don't know what you need to do to earn one. His eye discipline during this interview is as impressive as you're going to find. Coach of the Czech National Football League FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem, David Oulehla, was given the nearly impossible task of remaining locked while the talented reporter Sabina Jaksova interviewed him following a loss. I can't tell you what either of them are saying, so I don’t know for certain how well he answered the questions being lobbed his way over the reporter's visible and ample chest, but I can tell you what he was thinking. CAMERAMAN GETS CAUGHT RISKING IT ALL TO FILM WORLD CUP'S 'SEXIEST FAN' IN THE FORMULA 1 PADDOCK The last thing the coach wanted to do was add to the loss on the field with one off of it. He spent a lot of the interview staring straight ahead or down at the ground. He didn’t want to get caught gazing at the reverse mullet of outfits. Jaksova went business in the back, with a suit jacket and party in the front with a low-cut top. Coach was in a no-win situation and took the tie rather than the loss by staying focused and nailing the interview. If he was caught looking, the internet would have been all over him. If he didn’t, the interview would be relatable enough to go viral, which it did. It's pinned and sitting at almost 2 million views on the team's TikTok account. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! If your radar is going off here, you're tuned in to how the world works these days. Jaksova isn't the only hot reporter employed by the soccer team and, according to Jaksova, they reached out to her. "The club’s management contacted me directly and made me the offer. I admit that I was happy and surprised at the same time," she said, according to the New York Post. "I thought about it for a while, but finally said: ‘Why not? I’ll try.’ However, I had no experience, so I learned everything along the way." The team took a victory lap on Instagram after going viral. They announced that they were taking the world by storm once again and even mentioned their marketing. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "FK VIAGEM ÚSTÍ NAD LABEM IS TAKING THE WORLD BY STORM ONCE AGAIN! Our club, led by head coach David Oulehla and presenter Sabina Jakšová, has once again captured the attention of international media!," they wrote. "FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem is once again being talked about and written about across continents! Our name resonates far beyond the borders of the Czech Republic! OUR MARKETING HAS BECOME A WORLDWIDE SENSATION AGAIN!" How dare they use one of their hot reporters for marketing purposes.

articles.title: Giráldez: “La competición ha comenzado de forma cruel pero es para sentirse orgulloso”
articles.standfirst: El técnico cree que merecieron bastante más
articles.summary: El técnico cree que merecieron bastante más
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez lamenta la derrota de su equipo, entiende que es inmerecida, cree que es para sentirse orgulloso de su equipo y confía en la clasificación. Mala fortuna: “Ha empezado cruel la competición. Llevamos dos partidos con muchas sensaciones buenas que se nos van, el otro día en el 89 y hoy en el 91. Hemos competido muy bien, hemos hecho muchas cosas muy bien. Es una pena”. Valoración del encuentro: “Estoy contento con el partido. El inicio de la segunda parte no hemos estado bien, nos ha faltado un poco de fuelle en los cambios para poder estar más certeros en los últimos minutos. Buen trabajo del equipo contra un equipazo”. Orgulloso: “Si fuese aficionado del Celta no me iría decepcionado. Es un Celta-Juventus. Me parece necesario que disfrutemos de momentos como estos y con un gran ambiente. Tenemos que sentirnos orgullosos de disputar Europa League por segundo año consecutivo ante uno de los mejores equipos de la historia”. Optimista: “Nos vamos a meter en la siguiente fase. No hemos merecido perder y es una pena irnos de vacío con cero puntos en estos dos partidos pero creo que el camino es este. Hemos competido muy bien en muchos momentos del partido, creo que dominando con situaciones de presión buenas, situaciones de bloque bajo buenas. Felicitar a los chicos y a levantarnos para el partido del domingo que está a la vuelta de la esquina”.

images.caption: Claudio Giráldez, dando indicaciones durante el encuentro ante la Juventus. Salvador Sas

articles.title: El Sevilla democratiza el gol
articles.standfirst: Hasta once jugadores han visto portería esta temporada
articles.summary: Hasta once jugadores han visto portería esta temporada
articles.body: Con los estrenos de Robbie Ure y Félix Correia, ningún equipo tiene tantos goleadores diferentes en las cinco grandes ligas. Si bien la visita del Sevilla al Levante dejó un sabor amargo, el empate en el Ciutat de València sirvió para certificar una de las principales virtudes que caracteriza al nuevo proyecto de Luis García Plaza: la fuerza del bloque. Hasta el momento, han demostrado que poseen la capacidad de convertir su ataque en una amenaza coral, lo que a su vez les otorga un buen abanico de alternativas a la hora de crearle peligro a sus rivales. Con las primeras dianas de Robbie Ure y Félix Correia en LaLiga, los hispalenses se han consolidado como el equipo con más goleadores distintos de las cinco grandes ligas europeas en la presente temporada. De los 13 tantos convertidos por el Sevilla en estas ocho primeras jornadas, hasta 11 llevan una firma diferente. Isaac Romero y Miguel Sierra encabezan la nómina de anotadores con dos goles cada uno, secundados por una nutrida lista en la que figuran Jon Guridi, Peque, Oso, Chidera Ejuke, Lucas Stassin, Juan Iglesias, Youssouf Fofana, Robbie Ure y Félix Correia. De hecho, el cuadro blanquirrojo lidera este apartado en las cinco grandes ligas europeas por encima del Barcelona con 10 y el Brentford, el Bayer Leverkusen y el Bayern de Múnich, que acumulan 9. Más atrás quedan los ocho goleadores registrados por los referentes tanto de la Ligue 1 (París Saint-Germain) como de la Serie A (Atalanta). La diversidad de recursos ofensivos del Sevilla le lleva a sostener una gran regularidad de cara a portería, pues ha conseguido marcar en todos los partidos disputados hasta la fecha. Además, cabe señalar que se ha puesto por delante en el marcador en seis de los ocho compromisos ligueros. Únicamente le tocó remar a contracorriente frente al Rayo Vallecano -encuentro que terminó remontando por 2-1- y contra el Atlético de Madrid (1-3). Los buenos números goleadores del Sevilla destacan sobre todo a domicilio, donde ha marcado ocho goles en cuatro partidos, lo que le ha ayudado a mantener su condición de invicto lejos de Nervión (dos victorias y dos empates). A pesar de sus dos últimos resultados, continúa firmando su mejor arranque liguero desde el curso 2021-2022, cuando el equipo dirigido por Julen Lopetegui sumó los mismos 14 puntos de 24 posibles.

images.caption: Isaac Romero celebra un gol con el Sevilla EFE

articles.title: Man United’s Martinez apologises for outburst after talks with Carrick
articles.summary: Lisandro Martinez meets Manchester United manager Michael Carrick before apologising for his criticism of the club.
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club’s hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials.

Martinez met Carrick and club executives after training, two days after saying the club needed greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level following Tuesday’s 2-0 loss .

“Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager,” Martinez said in an Instagram post, in his second statement since the interview.

“It was a very positive conversation where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.”

A club source said that any internal disciplinary action would remain private, adding that it had been Martinez’s decision to apologise publicly and that all parties considered the matter closed.

British media, including the BBC, reported that United fined the defender over the outburst.

Martinez acknowledged that his frustration following the defeat had got the better of him and apologised for choosing the wrong moment to air his feelings.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity,” he said.

“The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

The Argentina international had singled out director of football Jason Wilcox in the post-game interview, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe.

Martinez said his comments had not reflected the unity required at Old Trafford and stressed his belief that everyone at the club was working towards the same goal.

“Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that,” he said.

“I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition, bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.”

Martinez finished his statement by drawing a line under the episode.

“With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together.”

United are 13th in the Premier League after six games in their worst start in 40 years. They travel to seventh-placed Leeds United on Sunday.

images.caption: Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez was part of the Argentina side that reached the FIFA World Cup 2026 final [File: Jon Super/AP]

articles.title: Deportivo - Levante | Duelo de grandes pizarras en Riazor: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: Se miden dos rivales directos y dos técnicos que trabajan con variedad de dibujos
articles.summary: Se miden dos rivales directos y dos técnicos que trabajan con variedad de dibujos
articles.body:
Dos equipos diseñados para luchar por la permanencia se miden en Riazor (21.00 horas, DAZN en abierto y Movistar LaLiga) con la intención de sumar tres puntos. Ambos arrastran cuatro partidos sin ganar, con los de Hidalgo más cómodos en la tabla por su gran inicio. Es de esos partidos que al final de LaLiga puede valer cuatro puntos.

Cómo llega el Deportivo . Antonio Hidalgo llega con la baja de tres futbolistas clave como Aubameyang, Marc Casadó y Eddahchouri por lesión, más la de Lorenzo Amatucci por sanción. En el once hay varias dudas como la pareja de Giménez en el centro de la zaga o el acompañante de Nsongo en punta. El Deportivo afronta el duelo después de perder en Anoeta encajando tres goles por errores infantiles. El propio técnico asegura que en la máxima categoría los errores te penalizan más y pide más concentración a los suyos. “Esto es Primera división, hay que estar siempre concentrados y preparados porque hay más calidad y muchos mejores futbolistas”.

Cómo llega el Levante . El cuadro granota busca en Riazor la segunda victoria del campeonato tras acumular cuatro partidos consecutivos sin vencer. Situados en el precipicio de la zona de descenso, cuartos por la cola con seis puntos y un partido menos a causa de la suspensión del choque ante el Athletic, Luís Castro se siente confiado en el trabajo de todo el grupo. Con tan solo tres días de margen entre la última jornada disputada por el equipo valenciano, los azulgranas viajan con cuatro ausencias, tres de ellas por lesión: Etta Eyong, que ya ha conseguido entrenarse de manera parcial pero que todavía no está listo, Hugo Sotelo y Alex Primo.

El duelo del partido . Yeremay vs Brugué . El Deportivo, con Aubameyang lesionado, necesita más que nunca al extremo canario, que se estrenó de penalti ante la Real. Brugué, con tres goles y una asistencia, diferencial en los granotas.

articles.title: Vini toca fondo
articles.standfirst: El brasileño se sincera, admite que está lejos de su mejor versión y promete recuperar al futbolista que dominó el mundo del fútbol
articles.summary: El brasileño se sincera, admite que está lejos de su mejor versión y promete recuperar al futbolista que dominó el mundo del fútbol
articles.body: El hombre que dicta sentencia debe blandir la espada. Vinicius lo hizo durante años en el Real Madrid, donde convirtió las burlas en goles, las dudas y los errores en el combustible de una transformación que lo llevó a la cima del fútbol mundial. Ahora, el brasileño atraviesa quizá su momento más delicado desde su llegada al fútbol español. Por primera vez, su fútbol transmite una fragilidad que va más allá de los números. Un gol y tres asistencias en Liga dibujan una temporada muy por debajo de su nivel, pero lo más preocupante es la sensación de que ha perdido la confianza que lo convirtió en uno de los jugadores más determinantes del planeta. "Estoy enfadado conmigo mismo por no estar en mi mejor versión", reconoce. Siempre el primer paso para intentar dar la vuelta a la complicada situación. Por eso la frase retrata el momento de un futbolista que no se conforma con lo que ofrece y que parece consciente de la distancia que lo separa de su mejor versión. Vinicius no esconde su frustración... tampoco renuncia a levantarse. "Vini siempre vuelve y no tengo dudas de que voy a volver", asegura. Su promesa es rotunda, pero el desafío también lo es. Recuperar la seguridad, la determinación y la capacidad para desequilibrar que durante años hicieron de cada una de sus apariciones una amenaza para el rival. Y todo eso en medio de una sanción que le apartará de los terrenos de juego los próximos cuatro partidos ligueros. Su historia invita a creer en esa resurrección. Cuando llegó al Madrid, las dudas acompañaron a un talento descomunal que todavía no encontraba la manera de traducir sus condiciones en eficacia. Fallaba ocasiones, acumulaba críticas y se convirtió en objetivo de las burlas. Muchos dudaron de que pudiera alcanzar el nivel que se esperaba de él. "Cuando llegué muchos se rieron de mí y al final llevo más de 100 goles en el Madrid", recuerda tras dejar esa etapa atrás. Pero el pasado, que ayuda en un camino ya transitado, no soluciona nada. Y es que el problema ya no consiste únicamente en volver a encontrar la portería. Se trata de recuperar la convicción con la que encaraba, insistía después de fallar y asumía la responsabilidad. Y eso lo sabe Mourinho, que necesita recuperar a ese futbolista. El equipo puede arroparlo, el entrenador puede darle oportunidades y el entorno puede recordarle todo lo que ha conseguido. Pero nadie puede devolverle la confianza ni el atrevimiento necesario para volver a intentarlo cuando las cosas salen mal. Esa parte de la reconstrucción no admite intermediarios.

images.caption: Vinicius durante el partido frente a la Roma.

articles.title: Jonny: "Donde más cómodo me siento es como central en una defensa de cinco"
articles.standfirst: El gallego mantiene la tranquilidad pese a las cuatro jornadas sin ganar.
articles.summary: El gallego mantiene la tranquilidad pese a las cuatro jornadas sin ganar.
articles.body: Volver a Balaidos siempre será especial para Jonny Otto. Más después de la espectacular victoria del Alavés hace apenas seis meses, donde fue capaz de voltear un 3-0 para acabar llevándose tres puntos que supusieron un punto de inflexión. El futbolista gallego se encuentra feliz en Vitoria, donde disfruta de la continuidad que todo jugador reclama reconvertido como central ante los diferentes contratiempos del equipo vitoriano en esa posición. "Siempre estoy contento por volver a casa. Tengo el recuerdo del año pasado, que fue el partido más loco de la temporada. Nos dejó un buen sabor de boca, pero sabemos que no va a ser igual que el año pasado. Va a ser un partido de tú a tú que lo ganará el equipo que menos errores cometa", expresa. Jonny apela a la calma pese a las cuatro jornadas sin ganar. "El equipo y la afición estamos tranquilos. Estamos en un buen momento, aunque venimos de perder. Cualquier mínimo detalle marca las diferencias. No hay una necesidad de ganar, pero siempre tenemos el convencimiento de hacerlo. Estamos en el momento de querer ganar para afianzarnos en la zona media-alta de la tabla". Su polivalencia está siendo muy útil para Quique Sánchez Flores a la hora de situarle en diferentes zonas del campo. "Desde que era pequeño siempre he jugado en cualquier posición de la defensa y se me ha hecho fácil adaptarme. Me siento muy cómodo en cualquiera de los laterales y central, pero si tengo que decantarme por una, creo que donde mejor me siento es como central en una defensa de cinco", confiesa Jonny. Todas las victorias del Alavés, hasta ahora, se han producido en Mendizorroza, aunque la plantilla mantiene la confianza intacta cuando juega a domicilio. "Los puntos cuentan igual en casa que fuera. La meta siempre es ganar, más allá del rival y el campo. Para estar en la zona media-alta el objetivo es ganar todos los partidos. Nos tenemos que acostumbrar a ganar e ir a por más".

images.caption: Jonny Otto intenta robar ante Sancet MARCA

articles.title: Alabama Responds After Fan Shoves Georgia's Raylen Wilson in Viral Video After Crimson Tide Loss
articles.summary: Alabama has publicly responded after a man was seen hitting Georgia linebacker Raylen Wilson while telling him to "get the f--k out of here" in a video following Saturday's 20-17 loss against the Bulldogs at Bryant-Denny Stadium.
articles.body:
Alabama has publicly responded after a man was seen hitting Georgia linebacker Raylen Wilson while telling him to "get the f--k out of here" in a video following Saturday's 20-17 loss against the Bulldogs at Bryant-Denny Stadium.

"Alabama has identified and taken appropriate action against the individual involved in videos circulating on social media following Saturday night's football game," the school said in a statement. "We take matters of this nature seriously and will not tolerate this behavior."

Georgia head coach Kirby Smart also addressed the situation on Monday.

"You want people to make good decisions and do things the right way," he told reporters. "Raylen certainly did there. There's so much that goes into that. He thought it was a Georgia fan. Probably helped him react the way he did initially. Disappointing behavior by any fan. Certainly nothing we condone and I'm sure Alabama doesn't condone it either."

Georgia jumped to No. 1 in the AP poll with the win (and with the help of a Texas loss), while Alabama remained at No. 6.

Alabama will be on the road against Tennessee this week, with it's next home game coming against Texas A&M on Oct. 24.

articles.title: Filipe Coelho: “Intentamos mantener el resultado, pero ellos marcaron un golazo”
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón analizó el empate en Rumanía en sala de prensa
articles.summary: El técnico azulón analizó el empate en Rumanía en sala de prensa
articles.body: El entrenador del Universitatea Craiova, Filipe Coelho, analizó en sala de prensa el empate frente al Getafe y señaló que el equipo buscó mantener la ventaja tras el primer gol, pero que el golazo de Gudelj desbarató las opciones del conjunto rumano de llevarse los primeros tres puntos en la Conference League. Valoración: “Creo que jugamos muy bien contra un buen equipo; un equipo que se enfrentó al Barcelona hace apenas unos días. Jugamos bien, marcamos el primer gol e intentamos mantener el resultado, pero luego ellos anotaron ese golazo”. Empate: “Este es nuestro primer punto. Los habíamos analizado y sabíamos cómo presionan; es un equipo que practica una presión alta. Intentamos atraerlos para jugar al contraataque y, por momentos, se nos abrieron espacios. Además, cometieron faltas para romper nuestro ritmo, Sucedió exactamente como esperábamos. Estoy orgulloso del desempeño de mis jugadores, tanto para el Craiova como para Rumanía. Ocasiones falladas: “No me molesta que un jugador falle. Estaba en la posición correcta e intentó definir. Assad cuenta con todo mi apoyo”. Resultado final: “Empezamos la segunda parte muy bien, con mucha valentía. Algunos de nuestros jugadores se cansaron durante la segunda mitad, y fue entonces cuando encajamos el gol. Debemos analizar el partido y ver qué podríamos haber hecho mejor en esa situación. Ellos no hicieron nada especialmente extraordinario”.

images.caption: Filipe Coelho, durante el partido ante el Getafe EFE

articles.title: Winners and Losers of a College Football Playoff 24-Team Expansion
articles.summary: Whether you're ready to fully embrace it or not, the College Football Playoff will likely soon grow larger.
articles.body:
Whether you're ready to fully embrace it or not, the College Football Playoff will likely soon grow larger.

In fact, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel , it's about to double in size. A new deal regarding the size and construction of the playoff is well in the works, and a 24-team playoff is likely to be finalized soon, replacing the current 12-team model.

Oh, and it will go into effect for the 2027 season if things trend in the direction that they are right now.

The impacts of such a decision are likely to be seismic in nature, and they will stretch well beyond how and when a postseason is played. From regular season games to conference championships, the entire sport is likely to undergo a major overhaul.

According to Pete Nakos on On3.com, the top eight teams are likely to receive first-round byes with 19 teams receiving at-large bids. The top four Power Four teams would receive an automatic bid, as would the highest-ranked Group of Six conference champion.

In addition, two rounds of playoff games would rather than one. The remaining rounds would be played on neutral sites.

The announcement of the imminent move has generated a flurry of strong opinions on its pending existence. As for what it means, here's a look at some of the winners and losers of a 24-team postseason.

There is no shortage of teams that regularly find themselves in and around the Top 25. Heck, many of these teams often flirt with placement in the top 15, only to eventually find ways to miss the College Football Playoff.

Under Kirk Ferentz, the Hawkeyes have been a beacon of college football consistency, even if the offense has often been on the wrong side of many jokes. Iowa has flirted with College Football Playoff inclusion, and it is doing so once again in 2026.

The team doesn't have the resources to regularly compete with the juggernauts of the CFB world, although it does plenty with less. As a result, there is a ceiling on Iowa's potential. The 12-team playoff has proven to be that ceiling, at least thus far.

For starving fan bases, the 24-team playoff offers hope and opportunity. Teams in need of near perfection will soon be given the gift of access, and it will change the expectations for these teams, the hope fan bases bring into each August, and perhaps the way these teams operate in the offseason.

Increasing access works in different directions. For many, however, a new path to a national championship, whether it's real or not, will suddenly take shape.

Make no mistake about it; those early college football games that used to define a team's season, the ones that could end (or at least put a dent in) a postseason resume, will mean a lot less than they used to.

There's no getting around it. When teams like Ohio State and Texas meet up early in the season, the outcome of that game will mean less than it once did.

That doesn't necessarily mean these games don't matter; it also doesn't mean we won't watch. If there is any positive to draw from this reality, the hope is that we will see more meaningful out-of-conference games scheduled because of the 24-team playoff.

Still, those games will never be as important as they are right now. The reason those games matter is that the stakes still feel high. Even at 12 teams, programs aren't gifted a slew of mulligans. In the current system, your third loss has eliminated you from contention.

But now? Everything changes. You can lose that important, high-profile regular season game and still find yourself comfortably in the postseason.

While the atmosphere on college football campuses will still make these games feel vibrant and significant, the outcomes of these games will mean less, and thus we will care less. Period.

For those teams playing football outside of the four major conferences, playoff access has been hard to come by. In fact, let's take that notion a step further.

In many instances, the CFB Playoff committee has largely penalized these teams whenever possible, even if the playoff saw two schools—James Madison and Tulane—crash the 12-team bracket in 2025. A lot needed to happen for these teams to breakthrough in 2025; a lot less will need to happen moving forward.

The SEC, Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC will still occupy the overwhelming majority of vacancies in each 24-team bracket, much like they do in a 12-team bracket.

That part won't change, even if we've seen exceptions. But with 12 additional spots to fill, the likelihood of teams creeping their way into this discussion just got significantly more reasonable.

One Group of Six team is guaranteed to be included in the top 25; this much we know. In most years, excluding what we saw in 2025, this would likely be it. With the field about to double, that is no longer the case.

While Group of Six teams will still be in the minority, the possibilities for so many schools just became real.

Hope. There's that word again. A lot more teams just got it.

Updated College Football Playoff Predictions

Loser: Conference Championship Game Enthusiasts

Barring something unforeseen, the 24-team playoff will mark the end of the majority of conference championships as we know it.

With the expanded playoff set to dominate the calendar and December and January, something will have to budge. And it seems like many—if not all—of these conference championship games will be the first to go.

In the 12-team playoff era, conference championship games have undoubtedly been overshadowed by the looming reality of the bracket being filled. In many respects, with or without expansion, the future of these title games have been in doubt for some time now.

It was simply a matter of when. And now, it appears we have our answer.

Those who appreciate the sport's history and nostalgia are likely to still carry a deep appreciation for what these games have meant over time. Even now, watching two exceptional teams compete for conference superiority has mattered.

The games, even if the postseason stakes were limited or nonexistent, mattered.

Now, however, those games are likely to be a thing of the past, which begs a different question: how will these automatic bids be decided? And given the size and scheduling discrepancies across these conferences, what will this process look like?

At the very least, a conference championship game gave us a definitive answer. Now, things just got a lot more cluttered.

In its current state, the College Football Playoff did something extraordinarily well. And when the bracket moves to 24 teams, it will double down on a feature that has really carried the early part of each and every postseason.

More college football games on college football campuses.

It sounds simple, right? Play football games in places where football games are normally played.

The first round of the 12-team playoff was played in the higher seed's home stadium, and the results were a smashing success. If the early reports are accurate, the College Football Playoff's expanded postseason could feature two rounds of games on college campuses.

Whether you're ready to embrace an expanded playoff or not, this is a brilliant way to expand.

The 16 teams outside the top eight would compete in the first round, with the highest eight seeds hosting those games. In the second round, the top eight seeds would then get their turn at playing host, taking on the winners from the previous round. After this round, the remaining games will be played at neutral sites.

In the current 12-team format, the top four teams that earn first-round byes never have a chance to host. The following round moves directly to neutral sites.

The 24-team postseason will change the flow of these games drastically, putting an emphasis on the greatest commodity the sport has over any other sport on earth.

While the expansion of the playoff will be polarizing, this aspect of it won't be. More games in college stadiums will make for quite a scene.

As it stands currently, college football's bowl season was already on life support.

The NFL Draft opt outs, transfer portal and general state of offseason chaos has sent this yearly ritual into a great state of unknown. Some teams, like Notre Dame a season ago, skipped out on the opportunity to play in a bowl game entirely.

They are not alone. Other teams have opted out for various reasons.

The decreased emphasis on the bowl season was already well in motion, and this will only carry that momentum forward. One can't help but wonder how an expanded playoff will damage this part of the calendar.

In terms of math, 12 additional teams that could have competed in bowls will soon be playing in playoff games. While there are plenty of teams to backfill these vacancies, what will these games look like?

While many (including this writer) still deeply appreciate the bowl season in its imperfect form, this feels like a defining moment. Whether it means far less games or no games at all, something is likely to give.

Although it might sound strange, moving the bowl season to the start of the college football season should be on the table. If that sounds drastic, that's because it is.

The bowl season as you once knew it has been slowly losing steam. Now, it likely needs to be completely reimagined to survive.

articles.title: Southern Nazarene safety Tyler Ulrich dies less than a week after suffering 'traumatic injury' during game
articles.summary: Southern Nazarene's game against Ouachita Baptist was reportedly stopped for 45 minutes as Ulrich received medical attention.
articles.body:
Division II Southern Nazarene announced Thursday that sophomore safety Tyler Ulrich died less than a week after he was injured during the team's game at Ouachita Baptist. He was 21.

The school told WFAA 8 in Dallas-Fort Worth on Wednesday that Ulrich had suffered a "traumatic injury" during the game. Ulrich had been in critical condition and the game was stopped for 45 minutes while he received medical attention, per the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.

"This loss is deeply felt across our campus," the school said in a statement. "Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer during this incredibly difficult time."

Earlier Thursday, Ulrich's father Mark posted to Facebook that Tyler had suffered a head injury in the game and "we truly need a miracle."

"Our family is truly blessed to receive all the love and prayers for our young Tyler and we are ever grateful," Ulrich posted Thursday afternoon. "But as much support and love that was given, it is with a heavy heart I am writing to say the Lord called Tyler this morning at 11:13 a.m."

A GoFundMe for the Ulrich family had nearly $14,000 as of Thursday afternoon.

Ulrich had appeared in all six of SNU's games to date and was third on the team with 39 tackles. The Crimson Storm are 1-5 ahead of their scheduled game against Southwestern Oklahoma State on Saturday

articles.title: Bournemouth: Minus 17 to European dream for Cherries
articles.summary: It was a night 127 years in the making as Bournemouth added another chapter to their fairytale with victory in their first-ever European home game.
articles.body:
It was a night soundtracked by the Impossible Dream.

And it was no coincidence that was the song chosen at the Vitality Stadium before Bournemouth's first European home game in the club's 127-year history.

As supporters lucky enough to bag a ticket for the historic occasion waved flags to the Andy Williams classic, a giant tifo rose from behind one of the stands, bearing the words 'Minus 17 to European dreams. AFC Bournemouth, established 1899'.

As recently as 2008, a night like this would have been unthinkable for Cherries supporters.

Just 18 years ago, Bournemouth were facing the prospect of no longer existing.

After entering administration, the club were relegated from League One after being handed a 10-point deduction.

But that was not the end of their troubles. To be allowed to compete in the 2008-09 season, Bournemouth, then managed by Eddie Howe, had to accept a further 17-point deduction in League Two.

It left them at the bottom of the Football League and seemingly destined for life as a non-league side.

By the end of the season, the Cherries had not only completed one of the greatest escapes in English football history to secure a 21st-place finish and survival, but had also laid the foundations for a decade of success, which culminated in a first promotion to the Premier League in 2015.

Fast-forward to the present day and Bournemouth are making history for all the right reasons in the Europa League. Thursday's 3-0 win over Sturm Graz meant they became only the second English side to win their first two matches in a major European competition since Bolton achieved the feat in the Uefa Cup 21 years ago.

"It's a moment that will live long in their memories," former defender Joel Ward told TNT Sports. "The club should relish this night.

"The owner [Bill Foley] manifested this moment when he first came into the club. He set the standards for this club, he has invested a lot into it and he wanted to see this club in Europe.

"He got his wish, and they have certainly started incredibly well so far."

Bournemouth earn historic win over Sturm Graz

It was a night that always seemed destined to produce a fairytale storyline, such has been the nature of Bournemouth's rise since 2008.

At Wednesday's pre-match press conference, defender Adam Smith - the club's longest-serving player after initially joining on loan from Tottenham in 2011 - admitted he would never have imagined captaining the Cherries in Europe.

But there was more to come for Smith. The right-back earned his own piece of history by providing the assist for Bournemouth's first European goal on home soil, with Evanilson heading his cross home late in the first half.

"It's been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it, so we are very happy," Smith told TNT Sports.

"We had a chat with each other and we got a reaction today. That's an AFC [Bournemouth] performance right there."

Since making his move from Tottenham permanent in 2014, Smith has made more than 430 appearances for the Cherries.

In that time, the 35-year-old has helped Bournemouth secure three promotions, two of which have taken them to the Premier League.

When he was replaced by James Hill midway through the second half, the home supporters rose to their feet and chanted Smith's name as he departed the field.

"He's an example to everyone of what hard work looks like and the rewards that you get, even towards the latter stages of your career," added Ward.

"He's extremely professional, and he fully deserves the success he's getting now. Nights like this are what you live for. To walk out captaining that side is emotional and makes the hair stand up on the back of your neck."

'If we stick together and play like this... then we are hard to play against'

It was no surprise to see Bournemouth supporters remain in their seats long after the final whistle as they attempted to soak up as much as they could of a landmark night on the south coast.

For Marco Rose and his players, though, the focus will quickly shift to Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland.

Despite soaring to new heights in the Europa League during the opening weeks of the season, their Premier League campaign is yet to get going.

The Cherries sit 18th in the table and are one of only three teams, alongside Fulham and Tottenham, yet to win a match this season.

"If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans, then we are hard to play against and it's hard to beat us," said Rose, who succeeded Andoni Iraola in June.

"That's what we should take into the next game."

Bournemouth's remarkable story will enter arguably its most glamorous chapter yet when AC Milan visit the Vitality Stadium next week.

articles.title: O'Neill defiant in defeat but Celtic's 'flat-track bullies' fail another big test
articles.summary: Celtic have now lost two Europa League group games, as well as two derbies - but Martin O'Neill is adamant he can see positive signs.
articles.body:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill chose to focus on the second-half positives from his side's 4-1 Europa League defeat by Benfica and insisted they can still reach the knockout stages despite their slow start.

In stark contrast, Chris Sutton branded his former side as "flat-track bullies".

Celtic have lost four of their past five games. Every high-stakes match this term - both meetings with Rangers and both European outings - has ended in a defeat.

By the time their performance improved in Lisbon on Thursday, they were three goals down and effectively already out of the contest, hamstrung by their own sloppy mistakes.

Dane Murray upended Jhon Duran to concede a penalty inside four minutes, an error which characterised the first 45 minutes.

Sebastian Tounekti then allowed Alexander Bah to run past him for Benfica's second and goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo was beaten too easily as Duran scored the hosts' third.

Celtic suffer fourth defeat in five against classy Benfica

Visit our Celtic page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Camilo Duran pulled one back after the break and struck a post as the Scottish champions improved, but Vangelis Pavlidis struck Benfica's fourth late on to kill any faint Celtic hopes.

"Last thing you want to do is concede so early on," O'Neill said. "We could've capitulated, but I thought the second-half performance was terrific. We created chance after chance.

"The second-half performance gives me the determination... I think we can still qualify. We can still do it.

"We came roaring back. We could've scored a number of goals. I accept on the break they could have scored themselves, as they did with their fourth goal."

Even the most ardent Celtic supporters would struggle to share their manager's optimism given they sit 34th of 36 teams in the competition after two games.

Captain Callum McGregor admitted Celtic were masters of their own downfall in the first half.

"First half we didn't help ourselves," he told TNT Sports. "Unforced errors lead to the second and third goals and you have a mountain to climb.

"We know at this level if you don't look after the ball you're going to get punished."

'I'd pick Duran over Hogh every day of the week'

Although Celtic conceded four, the scoreline did not flatter Benfica. The Portuguese side created chances aplenty in both halves and hit the woodwork twice in addition to their four goals.

Celtic's lack of depth in defence was exposed once again in the absence of the injured Cameron Carter-Vickers as Gianluca Prestianni and Duran tormented the visitors' back four.

However, it is in forward areas where O'Neill perhaps has his biggest headache.

Club record signing Kasper Hogh was hooked at half-time and has now failed to score in 10 of his first 11 outings since joining from Bodo/Glimt in the summer.

Duran shifted inside for the second half and posed far more of a threat than his Danish team-mate.

"If I'm a creative midfield player and I've got Duran and Hogh to pick from, I'm taking Duran every day of the week," former Celtic midfielder Scott Allan said.

"He looks to get off the side of defenders, if you put a ball in the area, he's more likely to be alive to it.

"Hogh just isn't firing on all cylinders. I can take that if he's doing the other side of the game a lot better than he is.

"You can see why Martin O'Neill made the substitution at half-time and there's no doubt Celtic looked much better going forward."

O'Neill admitted he sees Duran as being better through the middle, when asked about his Colombian talisman post-match, but given Hogh's price tag he might not be inclined to pull him out of the firing line just yet.

"[Duran] has played wide at his previous clubs," O'Neill said. "But I personally feel his best position is through the middle.

"It's now a matter of us trying to fit him in and I think we can do that. It's a real battle for places now."

articles.title: How do you go from BCS nonsense to a 24-team College Football Playoff nobody wants? By not listening to fans
articles.summary: The drumbeat of playoff expansion began decades ago, but now, it's a different entity holding the drumstick and playoff expansion has spun out of control.
articles.body:
Almost exactly 15 years ago, college football reached the height of discontent with the Bowl Championship Series and paved the way for an entirely brand new postseason.

It was the first Saturday in November 2011. LSU had just beaten Alabama, 9-6, in an overtime game in Tuscaloosa that was ferocious, dramatic and supposedly definitive in terms of the national championship picture.

LSU won, Alabama lost, and that was supposed to be that.

But two weeks later, Oklahoma State — the team that had risen to No. 2 in the rankings — lost a double-overtime shocker at Iowa State. The circumstances of the game were noteworthy. When Oklahoma State's players woke up that morning, they learned that a plane crash the night before had taken the life of two Oklahoma State women's basketball coaches, prompting some discussion about whether the game should be postponed. And then as the game played out, kicker Quinn Sharp attempted a go-ahead field goal that went straight over the upright with 1:21 , missing by such a narrow margin that players who were on the field that night still argue to this day that officials got the call wrong.

Despite the asterisks attached to that result, the loss was punishing enough for Alabama to end up back at No. 2 in the BCS rankings by the end, edging out Oklahoma State by mere fractions.

For years, critics had pummeled the BCS for excluding teams that had done enough to deserve their title shot. BCS defenders argued that what made college football unique was the urgency of the regular season, where each week was akin to a playoff. The argument went on for more than a decade.

But when the 2011 season ended with an all-SEC rematch, passing over an Oklahoma State team that barely lost an overtime game played hours after a campus tragedy, the tide started to turn. If the sanctity of the regular season mattered so much, why did LSU need to beat Alabama a second time? Why was Oklahoma State getting screwed over by a computer formula that nobody really understood? Outside of the SEC, everyone else in college football was furious.

When Alabama won a 21-0 snoozer in the title game, the BCS' fate was sealed. The morning after the championship, commissioners from the Football Bowl Subdivision met in New Orleans and began paving the way for a brand new postseason.

Shortly thereafter, the College Football Playoff was born. It was a big step but also an incremental one, intentionally capped at four teams because inside the room, decision-makers understood that while the way their sport crowned a national champion needed to change, the sport fundamentally did not.

At a meeting in April of 2013, where many of the key playoff details were being ironed out, CFP executive director Bill Hancock made it clear that presidents and commissioners "have no desire" to go beyond four teams. The ethos in the room was clear: Move slowly, be careful, don't break what isn't broken.

So if you're wondering how, in the span of a dozen years, we went from that to the 24-team playoff monstrosity that was reportedly nearly done on Thursday , you're asking the right question.

With every change to college football's postseason — from the traditional bowls to the Bowl Alliance to the BCS to the four-team CFP to the 12-team CFP — you can look back at a moment when public opinion soured on the previous format and the sport's leaders were forced to react.

This time, they're giving fans something hardly anyone has asked for. And it comes with trade-offs that could fundamentally change the core product in harmful ways.

Even though the 12-team playoff has worked as intended, preserving the delicate balance between access and exclusivity, blowing it all up after just three years to double the size of the field was not inevitable. It was a choice first championed by Big Ten commissioner Tony Petitti, a Harvard-educated lawyer-turned-TV executive who spent much of his career in Major League Baseball and has demonstrated little interest in college sports outside of how much money can be extracted from it.

Which is, of course, part of the business. College sports are professional sports now, and money has never been more of a factor in every decision that tears away the fabric of what used to be.

In this case, the point of more playoff games is not merely the TV money that will pour into the coffers of the Big Ten and SEC. It is a concession to the pressure many power conference schools are feeling when it takes $30 million or $40 million just to field a competitive roster. How can schools in the middle of the power leagues justify that investment, year after year, if playoff spots are too precious and the decaying bowl system is no longer an adequate reward?

If you think about it, the reason the bowls/BCS endured for so long was that everybody got a trophy. A team here or there getting snubbed from the BCS title game wasn't worth blowing up the utopia of the masses.

Though bowl games were invented to juice the winter time economies of travel destinations and eventually became a symbol of grift and waste, BCS defenders got one thing right: The moment you introduced a playoff, it would inevitably grow because fewer people would be happy in the end. Ever since, the most important decisions in college football have been dictated by FOMO.

When you go back to the beginning and trace the entire arc of how we ended up here, it all makes sense. As much as you may disagree with the conclusion, it is all logical.

But for the first time in this transformation of college football's postseason, this evolution comes with tradeoffs. Big ones.

Sure, the conference championship games had gotten stale and won't really be missed. The bowl system was decaying on its own with more and more players opting out, so killing it off isn't that big of a deal. You can even find some positives in your typical Pop-Tarts Bowl matchup now being converted to a first-round playoff game.

Those things aren't going to fundamentally change college football.

Here's what will: When Missouri plays at Ole Miss on Saturday, everyone watching the game in the stadium and on television will understand that the loser probably won't make this year's CFP. That's a really big deal. Sports are the best reality show on Earth, and most of the time they rise to the level of the stakes. That's why when you watch an NBA game on a Wednesday in February and compare it to a first-round playoff game in April, they look completely different.

Human beings respond to urgency. You cannot create it where it doesn't exist.

In a 24-team playoff world, there will be no urgency in a Missouri-Ole Miss game in October, nor in the BYU-Notre Dame game this weekend, nor for Ohio State desperate to avoid a second loss at Indiana.

College football stakeholders understand that. They are simply betting that fans are so hooked on the product that they won't care in any of the ways that hurt their bottom line.

They may be right, or they may be spectacularly wrong. We'll see. But there's no debating how dramatically and suddenly they're changing the sport, and the question is whether the juice is going to be worth the squeeze.

Will the extra playoff money cure the budget disasters at power conference schools who are spending beyond their means? Will more playoff spots satiate the appetites of the sport's middle class that just watched Indiana leapfrog over them? Will a few years of first-round playoff losses make a fan base any more satisfied with its coach than your typical 8-4 team is now?

If not, we'll be back here in another few years trying to figure out how to stuff a few more teams into the already bloated postseason. And at some point, we may look back and realize that throwing the 12-team playoff era in the trash after just three seasons caused more problems than it solved.

articles.title: Tate Sandell building confidence after Texas game winner
articles.summary: Tate Sandell says making the game-winner against Texas can build confidence as he learns to respond to setbacks.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners got a massive confidence-building win against the then-No. 1 Texas Longhorns in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners beat the Longhorns , 27-24, on a field goal as time expired.

That game should boost the confidence of several players, including last season's Lou Groza Award winner, kicker Tate Sandell. He was excellent last season; however, he missed his last two field goals of the season against the Alabama Crimson Tide in the College Football Playoff. He then started this season 3-of-6 on field goals. However, he hit his last two field goals against Texas. One was from 53 yards out, and the other was the 47-yard walk-off.

Sandell said those field goals should help build his confidence moving forward.

"Sometimes I think you need to see one go through," Sandell said via SoonerScoop. "There are going to be patches, and it's about how you respond to those patches."

Sandell's performance against Texas could be the reset he needed after a difficult stretch. Making a 53-yard field goal and then delivering the game-winner under pressure showed he can still deliver in the biggest moments. For a kicker, confidence can be crucial, and those two successful attempts give Sandell something positive to carry into the weeks ahead.

Oklahoma will need that reliability as it builds on the rivalry win and pushes through the SEC schedule. If Sandell can maintain his rhythm and continue converting from long range, he could once again become a major weapon for the Sooners. Saturday's finish reminded everyone what he can do when the opportunity arrives, and Oklahoma will hope it marks the start of a more consistent run.

articles.title: Troy Aikman says ESPN seems to be going in 'different direction'
articles.summary: Troy Aikman has been vocal about not having another deal at ESPN. He says it looks like the network is 'gonna go in a different direction'
articles.body:
Troy Aikman sounds a lot like someone who believes the Super Bowl on Valentine's Day will be the end of his run with Joe Buck at ESPN and on Monday Night Football.

The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has been open about not having a deal after this one expires. His broadcast partner Buck recently got a six-year, $108 million contract from ESPN.

On Thursday, Aikman added more fuel to the fire ... twice.

He spoke on a radio show in Dallas first. Later, he added stronger comments to Jimmy Traina, podcast host/writer for Underscore Media.

Aikman spoke first to 96.7 The Ticket ESPN saying, "" There's probably a time and a place for all that ," Aikman said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be."

He then spoke with Traina, making his situation and belief quite clear.

Here's what Aikman said to me about ESPN : "It just seems to be where they're going - that they're gonna go in a different direction because there's been no talks, no contract negotiations. We're in a Super Bowl year. The Super Bowl is Feb. 14. My contract ends in March. It just doesn't seem logical that if they were gonna keep me, something wouldn't be in place before that."

I asked Aikman if it will be tough to work the remainder of the season given that he thinks he's gone from ESPN.

"The rest of the season will be fine. Excited about it. Looking forward to it. It's awesome that we got the Super Bowl. Not a problem at all."

What could be next would be a step in an interesting NFL analyst carousel in the offseason. And don't forget Aikman serves as an ongoing front office consultant/advisor for the Miami Dolphins. That team is in disarray and could look to overhaul its management team if the losing continues.

articles.title: Denver Broncos vs. Seattle Seahawks, ‘TNF’ Week 6 open thread

articles.body:
We've got a good one tonight, Rumblers! Week 6 of the NFL starts off with a huge matchup between the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks. Buffalo Bills fans should pay close attention to this one, with the pair of 3-2 teams part of Buffalo's schedule this season.

Despite their matching records just above .5000, the Broncos and Seahawks are both playoff favorites. Some would even place them in Super Bowl conversations. Seattle is the reigning Super Bowl champion, but they've played a tough schedule thus far that has them suddenly having to claw their way back in pursuit of the undefeated San Francisco 49ers.

The task is simple this evening, Rumblers: You're Seahawks fans. Either team winning improves the Bills' Strength of Schedule, but the Broncos losing further helps Buffalo with more important play scenarios.

Denver has struggled on offense for much of the season, and head coach Sean Payton took back play-calling duties from new offensive coordinator Davis Webb. After picking up an ankle injury in Week 5, wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is ready to go tonight. Seattle should do all it can to once again feature JSN, who is any offense's best friend — a true cheat code for the passing game.

With that, here's your open thread for Week 6 of Thursday Night Football . As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

articles.title: Troy Aikman doubles down on potential ESPN exit: ‘It just seems to be where they’re going’
articles.summary: Troy Aikman is sending a message to ESPN — two in one day, actually. A few weeks ago, Joe Buck appeared with Bob Ley at the Seton Hall Center for Sports Medi...
articles.body:
Troy Aikman is sending a message to ESPN — two in one day, actually.

A few weeks ago, Joe Buck appeared with Bob Ley at the Seton Hall Center for Sports Media and spoke about his relationship with Aikman, his broadcast partner since 2002, saying it's like a marriage.

Aikman and Buck may have a professional divorce in their future, too.

On Wednesday, Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported "tension" between Buck and Aikman stemming from "their respective contract talks," which came to a head in the form of "an argument" before calling the Buffalo Bills' win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football this week.

Buck signed a lucrative contract extension with ESPN last month, The Athletic reported , while ESPN remains noncommittal to Aikman beyond this season. Aikman and Buck have manned ESPN's Monday Night Football booth since 2022 .

Come Thursday, Aikman appeared on KTCK The Ticket in Dallas and addressed the swelling rumors. Aikman chuckled, and a loaded pause followed before he finally responded.

"There's probably a time and a place for all that to be discussed," Aikman said. "I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what's happened. I'll broadcast through this season, and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens."

"But I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be," Aikman added.

Later Thursday, Jimmy Traina followed up with Aikman on where he stands with ESPN, and Aikman doubled down on his earlier comments.

"It just seems to be where they're going — that they're gonna go in a different direction because there's been no talks, no contract negotiations," Aikman told Traina. "We're in a Super Bowl year. The Super Bowl is Feb. 14. My contract ends in March. It just doesn't seem logical that if they were gonna keep me, something wouldn't be in place before that."

When asked how his murky future may impact the remainder of the NFL season, Aikman said, "The rest of the season will be fine. Excited about it. Looking forward to it. It's awesome that we got the Super Bowl. Not a problem at all."

Aikman may be trying to create leverage with ESPN, as Awful Announcing's Drew Lerner notes here , but given the tone and persistence of his comments, the Aikman-Buck booth is increasingly likely to be in its final months.
